2.3.6.1-f11.accuracy_reason: 'Terrae filii' is a standard idiom for men of no family, and Maecenas and Agrippa are proverbial for great men and patrons.

2.3.6.1-f19.accuracy_reason: Horace, Epistles 1.10.8 reads 'vivo et regno, simul ista reliqui'; the participle variant is reported correctly.

2.3.6.1-f2.accuracy_reason: Heauton Timorumenos 210 reads 'periclum ex aliis facito tibi quod ex usu siet', matching Burton's sidenote.

2.3.6.1-f28.accuracy_reason: Erasmus, Adagia I.x.17 is 'Annosa vulpes haud capitur laqueo'.

2.3.6.1-f3.accuracy_reason: Phormio 241ff. is Demipho's speech, which opens 'quom secundae res sunt maxume'.

2.3.6.1-f7.accuracy_reason: Aeneid 6.103–105 are Aeneas's words to the Sibyl; the standard text has 'inopinave' and 'praecepi'.

2.3.6.1-f9.accuracy_reason: Nathan Chytraeus (1543–1598) published the Variorum in Europa itinerum deliciae in 1594.
